headline_marked: Over 5,000 jobless as [[S Alam shuts 11 factories]] in Chattogram
headline: Over 5,000 jobless as S Alam shuts 11 factories in Chattogram
summary: The industrial giant has halted operations across all its units in Karnaphuli upazila, citing raw material shortages and an inability to open LCs.
details: S Alam Group has shut down all 11 of its industrial units in Karnaphuli upazila of Chattogram, leaving more than 5,000 workers and employees without jobs.
The shutdown took effect on July 31, following the publication of termination lists on factory notice boards on July 30.
The affected units include S Alam Refined Sugar Industries, S Alam Steel, S Alam Cement, S Alam Vegetable Oil Ltd., and several other steel and edible oil plants.
A company official stated that the factories have remained largely idle because the group has been unable to import raw materials.
The inability to open letters of credit (LCs) since the political transition in August 2024 has led to a prolonged shortage of materials and the eventual suspension of production.
Despite the production halt, the company noted that workers had continued to receive their salaries and festival bonuses until the closure.
The group's operations have faced increasing pressure following the fall of the Awami League government, with the group losing control of linked banks.
The Anti-Corruption Commission and other agencies are currently investigating alleged financial irregularities involving the group and its chairman, Saiful Alam Masud.
caption:
Over 5,000 workers lose their jobs as S Alam Group shuts down 11 factories in Chattogram.

S Alam Group has shut down all 11 of its industrial units in Karnaphuli upazila of Chattogram, leaving more than 5,000 workers and employees without jobs.

The shutdown took effect on July 31, following the publication of termination lists on factory notice boards on July 30.

The affected units include S Alam Refined Sugar Industries, S Alam Steel, S Alam Cement, S Alam Vegetable Oil Ltd., and several other steel and edible oil plants.

A company official stated that the factories have remained largely idle because the group has been unable to import raw materials.

The inability to open letters of credit (LCs) since the political transition in August 2024 has led to a prolonged shortage of materials and the eventual suspension of production.

Despite the production halt, the company noted that workers had continued to receive their salaries and festival bonuses until the closure.

The group's operations have faced increasing pressure following the fall of the Awami League government, with the group losing control of linked banks.

The Anti-Corruption Commission and other agencies are currently investigating alleged financial irregularities involving the group and its chairman, Saiful Alam Masud.
